sources.entry: Tiledesk - All-in-one customer engagement platform from lead-gen to post-sales, from WhatsApp to your website. With omni-channel live agents and AI-powered chatbots (alternative to Intercom, Zendesk, Tawk.to and Tidio). (Source Code) MIT Docker/K8S

summary.one_liner: Tiledesk is an open source live chat and customer support platform with integrated AI chatbots, deployable with Docker Compose or Kubernetes/Helm.
summary.what_it_does: Tiledesk is a Node.js/Express live chat platform that combines human agent chat with chatbots for customer service across web, Android and iOS. Its chatbots are built once and adapted automatically to each channel, such as WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger and Telegram, supporting images and buttons where the channel allows. The README says it can connect external applications through APIs and webhooks, and deploy visual applications inside a conversation. The repository holds deployment code that starts the full product with Docker Compose (for trials) or Kubernetes with Helm (for POCs and production). The deployment bundles the Tiledesk Server, Dashboard, Design Studio, Chat21 components, a Web Widget, a MongoDB database and a proxy. The Helm charts are described as a starting template that users should adapt before production use.
use_cases: self-hosted live chat for a website
customer support with chatbots and human agents
multichannel chat across WhatsApp, Messenger and Telegram
connecting custom apps to chat via APIs or webhooks
how_to_run: Docker Compose: see the 'Development and trials' section of the README for the compose setup (link not included in the README text provided)
Kubernetes with Helm: see the 'Development, POCs and production' section of the README (link not included in the README text provided)
For production, connect tiledesk-server to an external MongoDB (MongoAtlas or a Replica Set) rather than the internal MongoDB container
notable: One chatbot script runs on every channel, auto-adapting replies to each channel
Full stack packaged as Docker Compose or Helm charts, including server, dashboard, Design Studio and web widget
Can deploy visual applications inside a conversation
Exposes APIs and webhooks for connecting external applications
caveats: Helm charts are described as a template and should not be used as-is in production; the README advises replacing the internal MongoDB with an external database
Enterprise-only Docker images require credentials obtained by contacting info@tiledesk.com
The README does not describe logging or monitoring configuration in the charts
keywords: chat with customers on my website
